method.decode: ffmpeg mono PCM 22050 Hz, first 120 s; source kept unchanged
method.onset_envelope: STFT: 1024-sample Hann window, hop 220 samples (~9.977 ms). Positive flux of square-root magnitude; bands 40–10000 / 40–180 / 180–1500 / 1500–9000 Hz. Light Gaussian smoothing. Normalize each band by its 95th percentile.
method.tempo_search: 85–141 BPM at 0.025 BPM, offset search at 6 ms, maximized mean broad-band onset energy at periodic pulses in 18–88 s. Four bands checked separately. Refined origin/period via Nelder-Mead on pulse indices 32–159 and 192–218.
method.independent_validation: Pick local flux peaks within ±40 ms of predicted grid. Huber line fit of time against pulse index; 212 matched events. Peak strength is detector output, not subjective loudness or verified musical downbeat.
method.segmentation: Compare waveform RMS and high-band flux in two-second windows before/after structural candidates; detect nearby local transient.
method.fps_quantization: frame = floor(time_seconds * 30 + 0.5); frame numbers start at 0. Frame 3600 is the exclusive video endpoint, not an actual picture frame.

limitations: Automated analysis only: no claim of having listened to or manually certified individual audible beats.
A stable grid is supported by repeatable transient alignment; four-beat grouping and its downbeat phase are editorial assumptions inferred from repeating structural events.
Half-/double-time tempo interpretations remain possible. Use ~109.17 BPM as the animation pulse convention.
Weak intro/bridge beats can have no prominent audible attack; preserve the grid for continuity without adding a hit to every pulse.
Detector resolution is ~10 ms; decimal timestamps do not imply equivalent musical certainty. 30 fps quantization adds up to 16.7 ms.
120 s is a hard editorial length; it does not land exactly on this pulse grid. Keep the final image to 120 s and fade audio to the endpoint.
